'''Jakku Raider Speeders''' were a model<ref name="BFII">''[[Star Wars Battlefront II]]''</ref> of [[landspeeder]] built from scavenged parts that were used on the [[desert]] [[planet]] [[Jakku]].

==Description==
The Jakku Raider Speeder<ref name="TFAVD" /> was a [[landspeeder]] built from scavenged parts that was then customized to survive harsh [[desert]] terrains,<ref name="Toy" /> but only a few were ever made.<ref name="BFII" /> They were [[Color|white]] in color, with two [[steering vane]]s at the front, and the [[engine]]s on either side of the rear. The driver's seat was located between the engines, next to a single passenger seat and beneath a corroded sunshield and rollbar.<ref name="TFAVD" />

==History==
In the [[Standard year|year]] [[34 ABY]],<ref name="SWGA">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''</ref> one such speeder drove past [[Niima Outpost]] on Jakku just as the [[scavenger]] [[Rey Skywalker|Rey]] and the [[astromech droid]] [[BB-8]] were arriving together. The outpost was attacked shortly afterwards by the [[First Order]] military faction, who were searching for BB-8.<ref name="TFA">{{Film|VII}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Jakku Raider Speeder was created for the film [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']],<ref name="TFA" /> which was released in North America on [[December 18]], [[2015]].<ref name="Release Date">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-episode-vii-to-open-december-18-2015|text=Star Wars: Episode VII to Open December 18, 2015}}</ref> It was first seen by the public in toy form as part of the [[Star Wars: The Force Awakens (toy line)|''The Force Awakens'']] toy line made by [[Hasbro]] and released as part of the "[[Force Friday]]" promotional event on [[September 4]], 2015. The toy was simply titled "Desert Landspeeder" and included a detachable [[laser cannon]] located above the steering vanes.<ref name="Toy" />

The speeder also appears in ''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens Immersive 360 Experience]]'', a promotional video for the film made exclusively for [[Wikipedia:Facebook|Facebook]].<ref name="360 Jakku Video">{{Facebook|username=StarWars|url=StarWars/videos/1030579940326940|name=''[[Star Wars]]''|archivedate=20160219052927}}</ref>

The speeder then received its full name in the reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: The Visual Dictionary]]'',<ref name="TFAVD" /> which was written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]] and released in conjunction with the film.<ref name="New Books">{{SW|url=news/a-galaxy-of-star-wars-the-force-awakens-books-coming-december-18-first-look|text=A Galaxy of ''Star Wars: The Force Awakens'' Books Coming December 18 - UPDATED!}}</ref> The speeder also appeared in various other tie-ins to the film, including the ''[[Jakku Spy]]''<ref name="JS">[[Jakku Spy]]</ref> and ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens]]'' non-[[canon]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]]s, the latter of which included it as an unlockable vehicle the player could ride.<ref name="LSW">''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens]]''</ref>
